overview.text: The Akhtyrka tradition centres on the Mother of God beside Christ’s Cross and the icon found by the priest Basil Danilov in 1739.

blocks.text: The selected eighteenth-century image presents Mary with crossed hands beside a smaller Crucifixion. Her covered head and the arrangement of the hands belong to this displayed example. It is a reproduction of a specific old Akhtyrka-type panel; later copies need not repeat every detail of the particular original described by a commemorative article.

blocks.text: The OCA recounts the discovery in grass near the church and a series of healing stories after the icon was cleaned. It records repeated investigations, a 1751 Synodal recognition and a stone church funded with Empress Elizabeth’s support. The church was consecrated in 1768. These are attributed events and religious testimonies within the source’s shrine history.

blocks.text: The OCA expressly notes Western stylistic features in the original it describes and says that original is not the image displayed on its page. That distinction matters for copies: the uncovered head or specific prayer gesture mentioned there cannot automatically be assigned to every Akhtyrka reproduction. Its printed July 2 commemoration is retained without creating a civil-date conversion.
